instrument1_watchedFailing.readingOfThatOutput: the instrument names lens-city-manager where lens-finance was expected, which is the defect, computed rather than described, from the byte-identical pre-fix inputs.
instrument1_watchedFailing.andItIsPERMANENTinTheSuiteToo: the temporary swap was only to produce red output for this artifact. The shipped test carries the failing arm permanently and in the SAME test as the clean arm: assert.throws runs the identical acceptance loop over the fixture and asserts it throws with actual ['lens-city-manager'] and expected ['lens-finance']. It is the same loop and the same expected sets, so weakening the acceptance breaks the failing arm as well. A clean arm and an injected arm in different tests let an unrun check and a passing check look alike.

otherGatesProvenAbleToFire_inTheSameTest: the paired-control divergence check: one lens id DELETED from the head script's copy is caught both textually (LENS != ALL_LENS_IDS) and behaviourally (?lens=finance stamps the wrong data-surface); one work id ADDED that the module does not know is caught both ways too; a changed fallback is caught.

the enumeration-in-step check: a sixteenth .lens section injected into the markup no longer matches the CSS enumeration, and firstPaintVisible shows the real consequence - the unenumerated surface is unreachable and Overview paints instead.

the value-to-id mis-map check: html[data-tab="review"] #tab-place is rewritten into a copy of the stylesheet and the extractor throws by name. This is the one defect an enumeration invites that a set comparison is structurally blind to, because both sets still hold the same members.
the infra.md revision check: the forbidden claim shape is asserted to match a synthetic line carrying it, so the negative assertion is proven able to fire rather than merely green.
the fixture freeze: sha256 pins over LF-normalized bytes, so regenerating the fixture from the fixed files fails loudly instead of silently turning the failing arm into a passing one.
